title: finding(devx): root `tsconfig.base.json` is extended by no package tsconfig — all 30 extend the root `tsconfig.json` instead
body:
Filed unassigned by the dev seat implementing objectui#9189, which had to answer "is there a shared base tsconfig?" and got two different answers depending on which file it looked at. Routing, `domain:*`, `type` and grading are the triage seat's to produce.

## The measurement

The repository root carries `tsconfig.base.json`, a full compiler-options base (strict flags, `declaration`, `declarationMap`, `sourceMap`, `isolatedModules`, an `exclude` list). Its name says it is the base every package builds on.

Nothing in `packages/` extends it. Measured at `c64975e9f`:

- all 30 `packages/*/tsconfig.json` spell `"extends": "../../tsconfig.json"` — the **root** config, a different file with a different option set
- `tsconfig.base.json` is extended only by `tsconfig.node.json`, `tsconfig.scripts.json`, `tsconfig.react.json` and `examples/byo-backend-console/tsconfig.json`

The two files genuinely differ, so this is not a naming quibble. `tsconfig.base.json` sets `noUnusedLocals: true`, `noImplicitReturns: true`, `esModuleInterop`, `declarationMap` and `sourceMap`; the root `tsconfig.json` sets `noUnusedLocals: false`, no `noImplicitReturns`, `jsx`, `noEmit: true` and the workspace `paths` table. A package that switched its `extends` to the file named "base" would be compiled under materially different rules.

## Why it is worth a card

The cost is a wrong answer to a question that gets asked whenever someone wants to set one option in one place. objectui#9189's ruling said "if a shared base tsconfig exists, setting it there beats per-package lines" — and the honest answer to "does one exist?" is *a file called that exists, and it is not the one the packages use*. Reading the name instead of the `extends` edges sends the change into a file that 30 of 30 packages never load, where it would be green, inert, and invisible.

This is an observation, not a breakage: nothing is failing today.

## Not a proposal

⛔ This card does not argue for consolidating the two, and the population question objectui#7212 raises is not settled here. Three dispositions all look reasonable from where the measurement stands — make the packages extend it, retire it in favour of the root config, or rename it to what it actually is (the base for the node/scripts/react tier) — and choosing between them needs the altitude call this seat did not make.

Reported from a Claude Code dev session, session id `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`.
